html:
SMTO-SKL-0137 — SMTO couldn't upload your file to Slack

GUID: 1ff5d811-8bd2-58b9-a61d-8ce0955e6792
Slug: slack-file-upload-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack refused the file while SMTO was sending it, so the file was not shared to the channel. Slack may keep an unused, unshared placeholder for it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the channel or thread in Slack to confirm the file isn't there. SMTO shares a file only after Slack accepts it, so it shouldn't appear, but checking avoids a duplicate.
  2. Check in Slack that the connected account is allowed to upload files to that channel. Slack refuses uploads where file sharing isn't allowed.
  3. Ask the Agent to upload the file again. The file was never shared, so a fresh upload won't post it twice.

What success looks like

  • The file appears once in the Slack channel or thread.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details, which include the Slack file ID SMTO received, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep re-uploading the same file over and over.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The binary upload to the Slack-provided external upload URL returned a non-200, non-5xx status after files.getUploadURLExternal allocated a file_id; files.completeUploadExternal was not called.

What this means

  • The upload transfer endpoint returns a non-200 response outside the separately classified uncertain server-failure path. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • The upload transfer endpoint returns a non-200 response outside the separately classified uncertain server-failure path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe transfer status and retained allocated file_id before another attempt.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the file_id recorded in the error details (files.info) before a new transfer; it was allocated but never completed or shared. Rerun slack.upload_file with the conversation file and exact channel_id/thread_ts once the cause (size, workspace policy or a Slack-side rejection) is resolved.
  • Inspect any returned file_id before starting a new transfer. Upload a conversation-owned artifact to exact channel/thread IDs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact file/upload state is reconciled before a deliberate replacement transfer.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
